message: What information is preserved when droplet diameter and flame diameter are reported separately? Explain the measurement methods described by the sources.
Does the same camera measure both, or are the diagnostics different?
Which measured quantity would be relevant to identifying extinction, and what limits are stated by the authors?
How do the sources describe the purpose of ground-based solid-fuel apparatus compared with space-based facilities? Preserve whether statements are objectives or results.
Which unreported conditions would prevent a recorded specimen size from establishing experimental equivalence?
Which documents or search avenues could help investigate fire signatures before ignition under reduced gravity? Keep possible searches separate from established findings.
Does a material offgassing requirement establish an observed combustion result? Explain only what the source documents support.
Which records report oxygen percentages, and what is missing before comparing them with partial-pressure measurements?
What limits do the original reports place on interpreting ambient pressure as a combustion outcome?
Distinguish a reported ambient temperature from flame temperature without deriving missing measurements.
Provide observed droplet extinction in Martian gravity at 81.6 kPa and 24.8 % oxygen.
Was its measurement calibrated under the same conditions?
